fieldValues.title: 4. Shape the work: what we tried and where we went too far
fieldValues.thinking_reached:
The ideal: A remedy becomes issues that anyone can pick up: grounded in a problem (a bug needs none), placed under its parent, small, planned and checkable.

What we have tried: The Answers line and grounding checks; Part of and sub-issues; Technical plan and Acceptance; size and complexity labels; clerk flow --chain and care; the steward's comments; issue templates proposed (clerk#224); the bug ruling (clerk#223).

Problems recorded here: SP-109, SP-108, SP-111, SP-62.
fieldValues.tensions:
- Line 1, Plan in full and file and start: too far toward both plan in full and file and start, by turns. 42% of 430 merged PRs had no issue (decision f799b6bc); on 2026-10-25 six issues were filed free-form and rewritten, and bugs were held to the problem gate (SP-108).
- Line 2, Local conventions and one shape: too far toward Local conventions. Up to six complexity labels for three levels, retired gate labels still in place, three words for who may merge (SP-111; cleaned up 2026-10-25).
- Line 3, Labels and text and linked records: too far toward Labels and text. The handbook: the link to the problem is a line of text, not a record; eleven gate labels were created and nine later retired.
fieldValues.unresolved_questions:
- The three tensions are a first pass: none has its four 2×2 cases or the cube filled yet (handbook, A domain's axes, steps 3 and 4).
- Is each tension orthogonal to the other two in this stage, and which pole is yang here: does it flip from the parent domain?
fieldValues.next_action: Fill the 2×2 cases from the stage's own history; then name the remedy that moves us back out of each shadow.
